glossary.fusion: Bones joining together into one solid piece, losing movement.
glossary.inflammatory back pain: Back pain from inflammation: worse with rest and in the morning, better with exercise.
glossary.spinal mobility: How well the spine bends forwards, backwards and sideways.
glossary.morning stiffness: Joint stiffness on waking that eases with movement; long-lasting stiffness suggests inflammatory disease.
glossary.Achilles tendon: The thick tendon at the back of the ankle joining the calf muscles to the heel bone.
glossary.chest expansion: How much the chest widens on a deep breath; reduced when the rib joints stiffen.
glossary.stooped posture: A forward-bent, hunched posture, the 'question mark' spine of late AS.
glossary.anterior chamber: The fluid-filled space at the front of the eye between the cornea and the iris.
glossary.fragility fractures: Fractures from a fall from standing height or less, a sign of weak bones.
glossary.MRI: Magnetic resonance imaging: detailed scan without radiation that shows early bone marrow inflammation.
glossary.pelvic X-ray: Plain film of the pelvis that shows the sacroiliac joints.
glossary.modified classification criteria: Criteria for diagnosing AS that require sacroiliitis on imaging plus clinical features.
glossary.lumbar vertebral bodies: The main block-shaped parts of the five lower back bones.
glossary.subchondral erosions: Areas where bone just under the joint cartilage has been eaten away.
glossary.SI joint: Sacroiliac joint: where the base of the spine meets the pelvis.
glossary.ultrasound: Imaging using sound waves; good for tendons, entheses and joint inflammation.
glossary.lumbar flexion: Bending forwards at the lower back.
glossary.ibuprofen: A common NSAID painkiller and anti-inflammatory.
glossary.naproxen: A longer-acting NSAID often used first-line in AS.
glossary.physiotherapy: Exercise and movement therapy to keep joints mobile and muscles strong.
glossary.biologics: Antibody or protein drugs that block specific immune molecules.
glossary.IL-17 inhibitor: A biologic that blocks interleukin-17, a key inflammatory signal in AS.
glossary.ophthalmology: The specialty that treats eye disease.
glossary.topical: Applied directly to the area, such as eye drops.
glossary.pathophysiology: How a disease process disturbs normal body function.
glossary.self-peptides: Small fragments of the body's own proteins.
glossary.misfolded proteins: Proteins that have formed the wrong shape and may trigger an immune response.
glossary.autoimmune: When the immune system attacks the body's own tissues.
glossary.synovium: The lining of a joint that makes joint fluid; inflamed in rheumatoid arthritis.
glossary.psoriasis: A chronic skin disease with scaly red plaques, linked to AS.
glossary.IBD: Inflammatory bowel disease: Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis.
glossary.cytokines: Signalling proteins that immune cells use to talk to each other.
glossary.inflammatory cascade: A chain of immune signals, each one triggering the next, that amplifies inflammation.
